exercise_solutions.part1_quantifier: possible unordered pair counts for an unspecified convex polygon, not one fixed regular/maximal count
exercise_solutions.upper_bound_proof: For each edge direction a convex polygon has at most one edge on each of its two opposite supporting lines. Thus each side belongs to at most one parallel pair and the count is at most floor(n/2).
exercise_solutions.part2_answer: No center of symmetry for an odd number of genuine vertices.
exercise_solutions.part2_proof: A half-turn permutes the genuine vertices. A fixed vertex would be the center; there the two outgoing incident edge directions must be swapped into their negatives, making the two edges opposite and collinear. That would be a redundant straight-angle subdivision, not a genuine vertex. Thus no vertex is fixed, all vertices occur in two-element pairs, and vertex count is even.
